claims.path: ibm-backside-polysilicon-gettering identity, description, classification, 1977 patent event and earliest_record
claims.reason: Hu US4053335A abstract, Fig. 1 and Examples 1 and 7 describe backside polysilicon impurity sink and comparative electrical tests; US grant/publication 11 October 1977 is the inspected public record, not the 1976 filing. IBM is identified as assignee rather than inferred host. No absolute priority asserted. https://patents.google.com/patent/US4053335A/en

Hu US4053335A abstract and Examples 1 and 7 and Holland 1989 pp. 538, 541 §§2–3 and refs 14, 18–20 each describe backside polysilicon impurity sinks. Holland specifies phosphorus doping and the additional back-contact role. Chen and Silvestri 1982 abstract and experiments provide an independently performed later test in a different process, but one author was at IBM and Hu was acknowledged. Shared principle does not assert transfer or identical full processes. https://dhkah.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/08/holland_nuclear-instruments-and-methods-in-physics-research-section-a_1989.pdf ; https://ir.lib.nycu.edu.tw/bitstream/11536/4954/1/A1982NS83700036.pdf

claims.path: berkeley-fully-depleted-back-illuminated-ccd candidate from detector process and added evidence
claims.reason: Holland et al. 1997 §1 names phosphorus-doped backside polysilicon getter; Holland US6025585A Example 1 explicitly describes a thick getter according to 1989 process, etched off before a thin optical back window. Neither establishes independent confirmation for the specific December 1996 prototype. Spieler §8.8 pp. 366–367 discusses broader high-resistivity integration and photodiode lineage, and was a participant in the 1990 integration work. Candidate appropriately remains open. https://www.imagesensors.org/Past%20Workshops/1997%20Workshop/1997%20Papers/40%20Holland%20et%20al.pdf ; https://patents.google.com/patent/US6025585A/en ; https://www-physics.lbl.gov/~spieler/misc_stuff/text/sent_02jul05/text_pdf/Semiconductor_Detector_Systems.pdf Independently read the original 1996 PostScript §§2–4 and ref. [2]: it cites 1989 at backside gettering, and reports removal of the thick layer for a thin optical contact. These overlapping-team accounts do not independently confirm the December 1996 telescope prototype.

claims.path: lick-ccd-data-acquisition-system identity, description, location, 1987 publication and earliest_record
claims.reason: Robinson et al. 1987 original abstract and publication metadata identify Lick, programmable controllers, serial link, UNIX acquisition/analysis, several CCDs and observing instruments. Stover and Allen 1987 pp. 877–879, Table I and Fig. 1 report a working photometer with most components of the standard Lick system, corroborating the hardware configuration but with overlapping authors. Initial operation is not dated. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19870065201 ; https://adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1987PASP...99..877S

Stover et al. 1997 §3.2 and ref. 3 directly identify the standard Lick system in the laboratory characterization of packaged CCDs and cite Robinson et al. 1987; controller amplified and digitized output. Robinson abstract and Stover/Allen 1987 describe the named apparatus. The 1987 sources overlap the 1997 author Stover and do not independently confirm its 1997 use. Accept only as a directly observed narrow instrument-use fact, not a consequential innovation, transfer or on-sky-use claim. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260660401_Characterization_of_a_fully_depleted_CCD_on_high-resistivity_silicon ; https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19870065201 ; https://adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1987PASP...99..877S The 1996 original PostScript §4, ref. [12] also reports the Robinson acquisition system in laboratory characterization; its authors overlap the later report.

Checked cited original accessible passages and metadata; the Robinson full paper was not available, so its abstract and independently accessible 1987 photometer report support only the claims stated. Lane correctly records source overlap, candidate status, and frontier.

claims.path: lick-ccd-data-acquisition-system unresolved earlier system and Lauer source
claims.reason: Original 1981 Lick Technical Report 28 title page and Introduction document PDP-8 based CCD data-taking and describe operating features. Continuity to the later UNIX system remains a question. https://mthamilton.ucolick.org/techdocs/LOTR/LOTR28.pdf

corrections: Changed Spieler locator from §8.9.2 to §8.8 pp. 366–367 and acknowledged his earlier collaboration; removed IBM host assertion based solely on patent assignment.
deferred: Independent confirmation of the precise 1988/1989 gettering method on the 1996 prototype and direct transfer of Hu’s full process to Berkeley remain unresolved. Earlier Lick PDP-8 system continuity to the UNIX system is not established. The 1987 and 1997 Lick papers share Stover; later use has not been independently repeated.
